title: The Whole Harbor Anew
premise: Silas Zhou, once the most celebrated wedding planner on the coast, walked away from love after a betrayal he's never named, rebuilding his life around a failing harbor inn and a rule of never planning another wedding. When a snowstorm traps him with Marguerite 'Rita' Voss—his former business partner, first love, and now the rival planner bidding to demolish his inn for a resort—the two are forced to share one roof, one generator, and twelve years of unsaid things. As the thaw comes, so does the deadline: Rita's company breaks ground in thirty days unless Silas can prove the harbor's inheritance is legally his through the grandmother who left it half-finished. In the end, Silas must stand at an altar again—not as a guest, but as a groom—and say the vow he rehearsed for a decade, choosing belonging over safety just as the bulldozers arrive.
about_author: Ulyana Crane is a former event coordinator who spent six years watching other people promise each other forever before turning those observations into fiction. She lives in a coastal town much like the one in this novel, where she collects tide charts and unfinished letters.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Twelve years after abandoning wedding planning, Silas runs the failing Gullwing Inn and catalogs his life in careful, risk-free increments. A demolition notice arrives from Voss Development. The beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signs the Wrecking Orders
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita Voss returns to Harbor Light to oversee the resort project that will make her career, telling herself the town means nothing and the man she left there means less. The beat: armor over guilt.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Ago, in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with flashback. He finds his grandmother's will and an old partnership contract with Rita's signature in green ink—their shared dream of a wedding venue on the harbor. The beat: grief rekindled into something sharper.

chapters.title: A Meeting Neither Wanted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas confronts Rita at the town hall; their exchange is all contracts and cold professionalism, but old shorthand slips through. The beat: sparks disguised as hostility.

chapters.title: Thirty Days of Weather
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. The forecast turns brutal; her crew urges delay, but the ground-breaking deadline is contractual. She books a room at the Gullwing—the only lodging open—to scout the property. The beat: fatalism with a flicker of hope.

chapters.title: Snowfall, Check-In, No Exit
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The storm closes the coast road with Rita already checked in. Stranded together, they negotiate a fragile truce over the inn's last working fireplace. The beat: forced proximity, mutual wariness.

chapters.title: What the Generator Hums
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Power fails; by candlelight Rita sees the inn as it was meant to be—a venue, not a ruin—and catches herself defending it aloud. The beat: nostalgia ambushing ambition.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wine, an old photo album, and the truth surfaces: they were engaged once, briefly, secretly, before Rita took the job that ended everything. The beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm Breaks Something Else
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They wake too close, retreat too fast. Silas throws himself into shoveling snow and avoiding eye contact. The beat: embarrassment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Clause Seventeen
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita discovers a clause in the will: if Silas hosts a wedding at the Gullwing within thirty days, the harbor parcel passes fully to him, voiding her company's claim. She must decide whether to tell him. The beat: loyalty versus career.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Alone, Silas admits what he never said when she left: not anger, but 'stay.' He begins drafting a letter he may never send. The beat: vulnerability breaking through pride.

chapters.title: An Offer Shaped Like a Trap
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rita tells Silas about Clause Seventeen—framing it as strategy: host a wedding, save the inn. Both know what it costs him to plan weddings again. The beat: uneasy alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Nobody Left to Marry
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The problem: no couple, no date, no time. Silas swallows his fear and calls old clients; every lead falls through. The beat: despair sharpening into determination.

chapters.title: The Runaway Couple at the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Two young elopers, stranded and broke, wander into the inn. Silas offers them a free wedding; Rita watches him come alive doing the thing he swore off. The beat: wonder returning.

chapters.title: Champagne in Teacups
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Planning sessions late into the night; Rita and Silas fall back into their old creative rhythm, finishing each other's floor plans. The beat: intimacy rebuilt through work.

chapters.title: Her Mother on the Line
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita's mother warns her the company will replace her if the deal collapses, forcing Rita to weigh love against the duty she built her whole identity on. The beat: pressure mounting.

chapters.title: The Dress in the Attic
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas finds his grandmother's unfinished wedding dress and the half-written letter explaining why she left the clause: she believed love needs a deadline. The beat: inheritance as blessing.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Strangers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The eloping couple's rehearsal dinner doubles as a town gathering; neighbors who once blamed Silas for closing the inn soften. The beat: community re-embracing him.

chapters.title: Rita's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita quietly stalls her own company's survey crew, buying Silas days but committing professional treason. The beat: love tipping past duty.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A near-kiss interrupted by the couple's panicked maid-of-honor. Both retreat, terrified of repeating the past. The beat: longing denied.

chapters.title: The Betrayal, Told at Last
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas finally explains why he stopped believing in weddings: Rita's father used their early plans to sue them both, and Rita chose the settlement over him. The beat: wound opened to air.

chapters.title: I Chose Wrong
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita gives her side—her father blackmailed her with her mother's debts—and admits she chose wrong and has regretted it for twelve years. The beat: mutual forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Wedding Day, Whiteout Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The elopers' wedding arrives with another storm threatening; the town rallies to decorate the harbor hall. The beat: joy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Vow He Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Watching the couple marry, Silas chokes up mid-toast, saying more than he intended about second chances. Rita hears it. The beat: public tenderness.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking Moved Up
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Her company, suspicious of delays, moves the groundbreaking to day twenty-eight—before any legal filing could complete. The beat: the clock becomes merciless.

chapters.title: A Plan Made of Desperation
chapters.summary: Dual POV. To satisfy the clause in time, they'd need a wedding at the Gullwing itself within days—with no couple. Silas stares at Rita across the ledger. The beat: the unspoken proposal forming.

chapters.title: Say It First
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita, unable to wait, almost says it herself—then loses her nerve when Silas mentions moving away after the inn is saved. The beat: miscommunication as crisis.

chapters.title: The Empty Chapel Argument
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A blazing fight: Silas accuses Rita of always leaving; Rita accuses Silas of hiding behind ruins instead of risking love. The beat: truth weaponized, then understood.

chapters.title: Cold Beds, Warm Kitchens
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silent truce; they cook together for the town's storm shelter, hands brushing, apologies simmering unspoken. The beat: reconciliation through small acts.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finally Read
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita finds Silas's unsent decade-old letter and reads it alone: 'Stay.' She weeps in the attic among the dress and the tide charts. The beat: heartbreak transmuted to hope.

chapters.title: Two Rings in a Biscuit Tin
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas retrieves the rings they never wore and asks the town matriarch to witness whatever happens next. The beat: commitment crystallizing.

chapters.title: Day Twenty-Seven
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With one day left, Silas stands in the empty harbor hall and asks Rita—not to marry him, but to let him say the sentence he rehearsed. The beat: the emotional summit approached.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Silas says it: 'I choose you, out loud, in front of everyone, forever.' Rita answers with her own vow. They decide to marry at dawn to meet the clause. The beat: climax of the heart.

chapters.title: Bulldozers at the Gate
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Dawn: machines arrive as guests gather. Rita walks out in her coat, resigns in front of her own crew, and bars the gate. The beat: duty definitively broken.

chapters.title: A Wedding in Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The town builds a wedding at impossible speed—the dress finished, the hall lit, the eloped couple returning as witnesses. The beat: communal triumph.

chapters.title: Vows Against the Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Silas and Rita marry on the frozen dock as the ice cracks toward spring; the signed marriage certificate triggers Clause Seventeen. The beat: climax and catharsis.

chapters.title: The Deed and the Demolition Order
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The lawyer confirms the harbor parcel is Silas's; the demolition order dies. Rita's company retreats, and her resignation becomes a partnership offer elsewhere. The beat: victory with cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita grieves the career she torched, then finds peace planning one wedding a season beside Silas—love as vocation, not sacrifice. The beat: bittersweet settling.

chapters.title: The Whole Harbor, Lit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Summer reopening: the Gullwing hosts its first full season, string lights over the water, the grandmother's dress framed in the lobby. The beat: restoration made visible.

chapters.title: Anniversary, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. One year later, Silas writes a new ledger entry—not small safe steps, but one large true line: stayed. Rita joins him on the dock as the tide turns. The beat: earned, quiet joy.
